services.name: Outpatient Pharmacy
services.shortDescription: Prescription collection, verification, queue support, and a safe handover of medicines.
services.details: The outpatient team checks the prescription, prepares medicines, confirms patient details, and helps make sure the right medicine reaches the right person.
questions: How do I know when my prescription is ready?
What should I bring when collecting medicines?

services.name: Medication Counselling
services.shortDescription: A private conversation about how to use medicines safely and confidently.
services.details: Pharmacists can explain how a medicine is used, what to watch for, how to store it, and when to ask for help. Bring your medicines or a current list when possible.
questions: Can someone explain my new medicine?
What should I do if I miss a dose?

services.name: Value Added Services
services.shortDescription: Alternative collection pathways designed to make medicine access easier.
services.audience: Patients who need a more convenient collection option
services.details: Value Added Services may help eligible patients collect medicines through supported alternatives. Ask the Pharmacy team which option fits your prescription and clinic arrangement.
questions: Is there a more convenient way to collect my refill?
How do I check whether I am eligible?

services.name: PRIC
services.shortDescription: Pharmacy support that helps patients understand and use medicines throughout care.
services.details: PRIC helps connect medication information with the patient’s care journey. The team can help clarify medicine-related concerns and identify the next safe question to ask.
questions: Who can help me understand all my medicines together?

services.name: Inpatient & Discharge Pharmacy
services.shortDescription: Medication support for wards and the transition from hospital to home.
services.audience: Inpatients and patients preparing for discharge
services.details: Pharmacy teams support medication use during admission and help patients leave with clearer instructions, reconciled medicines, and a safer transition home.
questions: What changed in my medicines before I go home?
Who should I contact if I am unsure after discharge?

services.name: Clinical Pharmacy
services.shortDescription: Pharmacists working with the care team to optimise medication use.
services.audience: Patients receiving complex or specialised care
services.details: Clinical pharmacists collaborate with doctors, nurses, and other professionals to support safe, effective, and appropriate medication use for individual patients.
questions: Can a pharmacist review my medicines with the care team?

services.name: Pharmacy Logistics
services.shortDescription: The behind-the-scenes work that keeps patient medicines available and of good quality.
services.audience: Every patient who depends on a continuous supply
services.details: From forecasting and storage to distribution and quality checks, logistics protects continuity of care: ubat patient yang tidak putus dan berkualiti.
questions: How does the Pharmacy keep medicines available?

services.name: Medication Safety
services.shortDescription: Practical habits that reduce medicine errors at home and in the hospital.
services.audience: Everyone who uses or looks after medicines
services.details: Use medicines only as labelled or explained by a healthcare professional. Keep an updated medicine list, store products as directed, and ask before combining medicines or supplements.
questions: Can I take two pain relievers together?
What should I do if I think I have taken the wrong medicine?
